paper_metadata.title: Influence Mechanism of γ/γ' Phase Dissolution on Microstructural Characteristics and Creep Properties of Ni-Based Single-Crystal Superalloys at 1200 °C
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: Ni-based single-crystal superalloys
A c/C213-rich superalloy is prone to topological inversion at high temperatures, which negatively affects the creep properties of superalloys (Ref 8, 11).
Herein, the inﬂuence mechanism of c/C213phase dissolution on the microstructural characteristics and creep properties of Ni-based SC superalloys at 1200 /C176 C was investigated.

SC alloys were prepared in a vacuum induction melting furnace.
SC rods were prepared using a DZG-0.025 directional solidification furnace.
The superalloy rods were heat-treated at 1320 °C/1 h + 1325 °C/2 h + 1330 °C/2 h + 1335 °C/2 h + 1345 °C/10 h, AC + 1160 °C/2 h, AC + 870 °C/32 h, and AC.
After the heat treatment, the SC samples were isothermally heat-treated at 1200 °C with holding times of 0–10 h to analyze the evolution of their microstructures.
Creep tests were performed at 1200 °C/80 MPa for the SC rods with orientations within 10° of the [001] direction.
